definition_zh: 山；山岳；山区；大量；巨大障碍
definition_en: a very high natural raised part of the earth's surface; also a huge amount of something or a very large problem
core_image: 平地向上隆起，越往上越窄，最后收成一个尖顶
scene: 清晨的云层压在半山腰，登山者沿着碎石坡继续向上。A cold wind sweeps across the mountain before sunrise.
sceneCN: 此处指「高耸于地表之上的巨大自然隆起」（第 1 个义项：由地壳抬升与侵蚀塑造出的山体）；句意为日出之前，一阵冷风扫过这座山。图中可辨识物件：低垂的云层、碎石坡、登山者的背包、裸露的岩壁。

pos.zh: 山；山岳；山区（the mountains）；大量（a mountain of）；巨大障碍
山的；山区的（如 mountain road、mountain climate）

senses.title: A high natural elevation of the land
senses.definition: a very high part of the earth's surface that rises above the land around it
senses.definitionCN: 高出周围地面的巨大天然隆起
senses.example: Snow still covers the upper slopes of the mountain in June.
senses.exampleCN: 到了六月，这座山的上部坡面仍覆盖着积雪。
senses.why: The word names the physical shape itself: ground that projects upward until it narrows into rock and snow.
senses.whyCN: 这个词直接称呼那种形状：地面向上隆起，越往上越窄，最终变成岩石与积雪。

senses.title: A mountain region
senses.definition: the mountains, used in the plural for a region of high land
senses.definitionCN: 用复数指整片高海拔山地地区
senses.example: They spent the summer hiking in the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整个夏天都在山区徒步。
senses.why: One peak becomes a landscape when the plural collects many of them into a single place to live in or travel through.
senses.whyCN: 把许多山峰收进复数，单一的山就变成一片可以居住、可以穿行的地带。

senses.title: A very large amount
senses.definition: a very large quantity of something abstract, especially work or debt
senses.definitionCN: 某抽象事物的极大数量，尤指工作或债务
senses.example: A mountain of paperwork awaited her after the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 假期结束后，堆积如山的文件等着她处理。
senses.why: Quantity is pictured as height: the taller the pile, the more it resembles a peak the speaker has to climb.
senses.whyCN: 数量被画成高度：堆得越高，越像一座必须爬过去的山峰。

senses.title: A huge obstacle
senses.definition: a very large problem or difficulty that must be overcome
senses.definitionCN: 必须克服的巨大问题或困难
senses.example: The new rule is a mountain to climb for small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定对小企业来说是一座必须翻越的大山。
senses.why: What blocks a traveller is imagined as terrain: the difficulty takes the shape of a slope that has to be crossed.
senses.whyCN: 挡住行路者的东西被想象成地形：困难取得了一个必须翻越的坡面形状。

senses.title: A mountain-like mass
senses.titleCN: 巨浪；山一般高大的物体
senses.definition: something enormously tall and solid, such as a wave or an iceberg
senses.definitionCN: 极其高大厚实的物体，如巨浪或冰山
senses.example: Mountainous waves broke over the harbour wall.
senses.exampleCN: 山一般的巨浪越过港口的防波堤。
senses.why: The shape, not the material, is what counts: anything that rises steeply and hugely can borrow the word.
senses.whyCN: 起作用的是形状而不是材质：凡是陡峭而巨大地隆起的东西，都可以借这个词。

senses.title: A piled-up heap
senses.definition: a heap of physical things piled higher than a person can easily deal with
senses.definitionCN: 堆得高到难以处理的实物堆
senses.example: A mountain of sand blocked the drain behind the house.
senses.exampleCN: 一堆沙子堵住了屋后的排水口。
senses.why: Here the metaphor becomes literal again: the heap really does have slopes and a top, like a small peak.
senses.whyCN: 这里比喻又落回字面：这堆东西真的有坡面、有顶端，像一座小山峰。

senses.title: Attributive: belonging to the mountains
senses.definition: used before another noun to mean of, on or typical of high land
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，表示属于山地或在山上
senses.example: Mountain roads close early when the first snow arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 第一场雪落下时，山路会提前封闭。
senses.why: English often lets a noun modify another noun; the first noun simply marks the setting of the second.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让名词修饰名词；前一个名词只是标出后一个名词所处的场景。

senses.title: Ski terrain at a resort
senses.definition: the slope or set of slopes that a ski resort operates
senses.definitionCN: 滑雪场经营的一片坡地或雪道区域
senses.example: After the first heavy snow the resort opens the whole mountain.
senses.exampleCN: 第一场大雪之后，滑雪场开放整片山体。
senses.why: Resort speech shortens the terrain to the noun: the thing being sold is access to the slope.
senses.whyCN: 滑雪场的说法把地形压缩成一个名词：出售的其实是进入坡道的权利。

intro.en: Mountain reached English through Old French from Latin mons, montis 'mountain'. The deeper Indo-European origin is debated, and the dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: mountain 经古法语来自拉丁 mons、montis「山」。更早的印欧语来源存在争议，以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin mons (genitive montis) meant 'mountain' and also 'a projecting mass'; the adjective montanus 'of a mountain' was formed from the same stem.
items.cn: 拉丁 mons（属格 montis）意为「山」，也指「突起的巨块」；形容词 montanus「山的」由同一词干构成。

items.en: A link with Proto-Indo-European *men- 'to stand out, project' is often proposed, but it is a reconstruction, not an attested form; some references leave the pre-Latin origin unsettled.
items.cn: 常有人提出它与原始印欧语 *men-「突出、隆起」有关，但这只是重构形式，并非有记录的词形；部分资料认为拉丁语之前的来源尚无定论。

items.en: Colloquial Latin built *montanea from montanus, a feminine noun meaning 'mountainous country', which passed into the Romance languages.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语由 montanus 造出 *montanea，这是一个阴性名词，指「多山的地带」，随后进入罗曼语族。

items.en: Old French montaigne, later montagne, continued the Vulgar Latin form and could mean both a mountain and a mound.
items.cn: 古法语 montaigne（后来写作 montagne）延续了通俗拉丁语形式，既可指山，也可指土丘。

items.en: English borrowed montaigne in the fourteenth century as mountaine; the spelling settled as mountain only in the early modern period.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入 montaigne，写作 mountaine；直到近代早期，拼写才固定为 mountain。

items.en: The figurative senses 'a huge amount' and 'a great difficulty' are recorded from the seventeenth century; the ski-resort sense belongs to the twentieth century.
items.cn: 「大量」与「巨大困难」的比喻义见于 17 世纪；滑雪场义则属于 20 世纪。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound close to mountain; the second holds words for raised land that differ in size or profile.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近的词；第二组是同样表示隆起地形、但在尺度或轮廓上不同的词。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to climb or get on, and a noun used before names such as Mount Everest; it came through French monter rather than from the noun mountain.
entries.definitionCN: 动词表示登上、骑上，名词用于 Mount Everest 一类专名；它经法语 monter 传入，并非由名词 mountain 派生。

entries.definition: A low pile or small hill; it goes back to Old English mund 'protection, hand', not to Latin mons.
entries.definitionCN: 低矮的土堆或小丘；它源自古英语 mund「保护、手」，与拉丁 mons 无关。

entries.definition: A quantity or total; historically it goes back to Latin ad montem 'to the hill', so it is distantly related in form but means quantity, not terrain.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或总额；历史上溯至拉丁 ad montem「到山上去」，形式上远亲，但意思指数量，不指地形。

entries.definition: A person who climbs mountains; it is mountain plus -eer, so it is a derivative rather than a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 登山者；由 mountain 加 -eer 构成，属于派生词，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: Raised land smaller and gentler than a mountain, usually under a few hundred metres; the boundary with mountain is conventional rather than natural.
entries.definitionCN: 比山更小、更平缓的隆起地形，通常只有几百米高；它与 mountain 的分界是习惯约定，而非自然界限。

entries.definition: The pointed top of a mountain, not the whole mass; a peak is what you reach, a mountain is what you climb.
entries.definitionCN: 指山峰的尖顶，而不是整座山体；peak 是你抵达的那个点，mountain 是你攀爬的整座东西。

entries.definition: The highest point of a mountain or of a career; it is more formal than peak and often used of reaching it.
entries.definitionCN: 山或事业的最高点；比 peak 更正式，常用于「登顶」的语境。

entries.definition: The measured height of land above sea level, or a raised area in general; it is a technical measure, not a landscape word.
entries.definitionCN: 海拔高度，或泛指高地；它是一个技术性的量度，不是地貌词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin stem, the real derivative family and the fixed phrases that mark each sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词干、真实的派生词族，以及标记各个义项的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin mons, montis 'mountain' gives the stem mont-, seen in montane, montanus and promontory.
normal.cn: 拉丁 mons、montis「山」给出词干 mont-，见于 montane、montanus 与 promontory。

normal.en: The family runs mountain, mountainous, mountaineer, mountaineering, mountainside.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mountain、mountainous、mountaineer、mountaineering、mountainside。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: mountain range, mountain peak, a mountain of work, a mountain to climb.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：mountain range、mountain peak、a mountain of work、a mountain to climb。

normal.en: The plural is a place: to go into the mountains is to enter a region, not to visit one peak.
normal.cn: 复数指一片地方：go into the mountains 是进入一片山区，而不是去看一座峰。

normal.en: Height supplies the metaphor: more work is a taller pile, a harder task is a steeper climb.
normal.cn: 高度提供比喻：工作越多，堆得越高；任务越难，坡越陡。

abstract.en: Picture a flat sheet pushed up from below until it folds into a point.
abstract.cn: 想象一张平板被从下面顶起，直到折成一个尖。

abstract.en: Picture a desk where every new sheet of paper raises the pile by one more centimetre.
abstract.cn: 想象一张书桌，每来一张纸，纸堆就再高一厘米。

abstract.en: Picture a wall that grows taller each time you finish a task, instead of shorter.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙，你每完成一件事它就更高，而不是更矮。

examples.en: The village sits at the foot of a mountain that is snow-covered for eight months.
examples.cn: 这个村庄坐落在一座每年有八个月积雪的山脚下。

examples.en: She came back from the conference with a mountain of new contacts.
examples.cn: 她从会议回来时带回了一大批新联系人。

examples.en: Getting the permit approved turned out to be a mountain of paperwork.
examples.cn: 把许可证批下来，结果成了一座文件大山。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「冒（mau）+ 天（ntain）」—— 从地面冒出来、一直顶到天的大土堆 → 山

root: 拉丁 mons、montis「山」，形容词 montanus「山的」；更早的印欧来源存疑，常被重构为 *men-「突出」，属假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shape: ground rises, narrows to a top, becomes a region, and then lends its height to amounts, obstacles, huge masses, heaps and ski slopes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形状展开：地面隆起、收成顶端、成为一片地区，再把这种高度借给数量、障碍、巨物、实物堆与滑雪坡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: flat ground lifted into a steep mass that ends in a point.
core.cn: 核心意象：平地被抬起，形成陡峭的巨块，最后收成一个尖顶。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL SHAPE: a single raised mass, and the same noun used to mark mountain settings.
branches.cn: 实体形状：单一隆起的巨块，以及用同一名词标出山地场景的定语用法。

branches.en: THE REGION: the plural turns many peaks into one habitable highland.
branches.cn: 整片地区：复数把许多峰收成一片可居住的高地。

branches.en: HEIGHT AS QUANTITY: abstract amounts and real heaps both borrow the profile of a peak.
branches.cn: 高度即数量：抽象的数量与实物的堆都借用了山峰的轮廓。

branches.en: HEIGHT AS DIFFICULTY: what must be overcome takes the shape of a slope.
branches.cn: 高度即困难：必须克服的东西取得坡面的形状。

branches.en: BORROWED TERRAIN: waves, icebergs and ski slopes are called mountains because they rise like one.
branches.cn: 借来的地形：巨浪、冰山与雪道被称作山，是因为它们像山一样隆起。

intro.en: Mountain is a Romance loan whose Latin stem mont- still builds technical and place words in English.
intro.cn: mountain 是罗曼语借词，其拉丁词干 mont- 在英语中仍能构成技术词与地名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin mons, montis and its adjective montanus supply the stem for montane, promontory and the Romance words for mountain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mons、montis 及其形容词 montanus 为 montane、promontory 以及罗曼语族的「山」提供词干。

items.example: The stem mont- appears in several English technical words.
items.exampleCN: 词干 mont- 出现在若干英语技术词中。

items.structure: Old French montaigne, from Vulgar Latin *montanea
items.meaning: a high raised mass of land
items.example: The mountain rises above the cloud line.
items.exampleCN: 这座山高过云层线。

items.structure: mountain + -ous (full of, having the character of)
items.meaning: full of mountains; huge like a mountain
items.meaningCN: 多山的；像山一样巨大的
items.example: The far side of the lake is mountainous.
items.exampleCN: 湖的对岸是多山的地区。

items.example: The mountaineer checked the rope twice.
items.exampleCN: 登山者检查了两次绳索。

items.example: Mountaineering demands patience as much as strength.
items.exampleCN: 登山运动既需要力量，也同样需要耐心。

items.meaning: the sloping side of a mountain
items.example: Terraces cover the mountainside.
items.exampleCN: 梯田铺满这片山坡。

items.meaning: the highest part of a mountain
items.example: Cloud hid the mountain-top all morning.
items.exampleCN: 整个上午云雾都遮着山顶。

items.meaning: belonging to a mountain zone, especially in ecology
items.meaningCN: 山地带的（尤用于生态学）
items.example: Montane forests begin above the valley floor.
items.exampleCN: 山地森林从谷底以上开始。

items.meaning: a high point of land projecting into the sea
items.example: A lighthouse stands on the promontory.
items.exampleCN: 一座灯塔立在这个海角上。

items.structure: Old French amonter, ultimately ad montem 'up to the hill'
items.meaning: a quantity; to add up to
items.example: The amount of snow doubled overnight.
items.exampleCN: 一夜之间降雪量翻了一倍。

latinEntries.meaning: of or belonging to a mountain
a headland, literally a forward mountain
latinEntries.meaningCN: 海角；字面义为「向前伸出的山」

definition_zh: 多山的；山区的；如山一般巨大的；艰巨的
definition_en: having many mountains; also enormously large, like a mountain, or extremely difficult
core_image: 一片地面上接连不断的山脊，几乎没有一块平坦的空地
scene: 车队沿着盘山公路缓慢爬升，两侧的坡壁一次次逼近车窗。The mountainous terrain makes every kilometre slow.
sceneCN: 此处指「地形以山地为主、坡多而少平地」（第 1 个义项：大片地面被山体占据）；句意为这种多山的地形让每一公里都走得很慢。图中可辨识物件：盘山公路、逼近车窗的坡壁、连续的山脊、缓慢行驶的车队。

pos.zh: 多山的；山区的；如山一般巨大的；艰巨的

senses.title: Full of mountains
senses.definition: used of a region whose surface is mostly high, steep land
senses.definitionCN: 用于地面大部分为高而陡的陆地的地区
senses.example: The north of the country is mountainous and thinly populated.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家的北部多山，人口稀少。
senses.why: -ous means 'full of' or 'having the character of', so mountainous is literally 'mountain-full'.
senses.whyCN: -ous 表示「充满」或「具有……的性质」，所以这个词字面就是「装满了山的」。

senses.title: Belonging to mountain life
senses.titleCN: 山区的；山地生活特有的
senses.definition: typical of mountain areas, their climate, roads or communities
senses.definitionCN: 具有山区特征的，如气候、道路或社区
senses.example: Mountainous villages often depend on a single road.
senses.exampleCN: 山区的村庄往往只依赖一条公路。
senses.why: Once a region is called mountainous, everything in it can share the label as a setting.
senses.whyCN: 一片地区一旦被称为多山，其中的一切都可以作为「场景」共用这个标签。

senses.title: As tall as a mountain, of waves
senses.definition: used of waves or water that rise to a great height
senses.definitionCN: 用于升得极高的波浪或水体
senses.example: Mountainous waves broke over the harbour wall.
senses.exampleCN: 如山的巨浪越过港口防波堤。
senses.why: Height is the shared feature: the water takes the profile of a peak without being made of rock.
senses.whyCN: 共同点是高度：水面取得了山峰的轮廓，尽管它不是岩石构成的。

senses.title: Enormous in amount
senses.definition: used of debts, costs or numbers that are huge and hard to reduce
senses.definitionCN: 用于巨大而难以削减的债务、成本或数字
senses.example: Mountainous debt forced the company to sell its factories.
senses.exampleCN: 庞大的债务迫使公司卖掉工厂。
senses.why: The metaphor moves from visible terrain to quantity: what is large enough to block the view becomes mountainous.
senses.whyCN: 比喻从可见地形转向数量：大到挡住视线的东西，就被说成如山一般。

senses.title: Huge and solid in form
senses.definition: used of an object that is enormously tall or bulky
senses.definitionCN: 用于极其高大或庞大的物体
senses.example: A mountainous iceberg drifted into the shipping lane.
senses.exampleCN: 一座巨大的冰山漂进了航道。
senses.why: Shape alone is enough: a mass with steep sides reads as mountainous even when it is ice, not rock.
senses.whyCN: 仅凭形状就够了：侧面陡峭的巨块即使由冰而非岩石构成，读起来也像山。

senses.title: Extremely difficult, like a climb
senses.definition: used of a task that is very hard and takes a long effort
senses.definitionCN: 用于非常艰难、需要长期努力的任务
senses.example: Reforming the tax system was a mountainous task.
senses.exampleCN: 改革税制是一项艰巨的任务。
senses.why: If a mountain is a great obstacle, then an obstacle of mountain size is mountainous in difficulty.
senses.whyCN: 如果山是巨大的障碍，那么有山那么大难度的障碍就是「如山般艰巨」的。

senses.title: Of mountainous relief, in geography
senses.definition: a technical description of terrain dominated by high relief
senses.definitionCN: 对以高起伏地形为主的地貌的技术描述
senses.example: Mountainous relief covers about a third of the province.
senses.exampleCN: 山地地貌约占这个省的三分之一。
senses.why: Geography uses the adjective for a measurable class of terrain, not for a single peak.
senses.whyCN: 地理学把这个形容词用于一类可测量的地形，而不是指单独一座峰。

senses.title: Huge in bodily form
senses.definition: a literary or informal use for a very large person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 文学作品或口语中形容十分高大的人或动物
senses.example: A mountainous figure filled the doorway.
senses.exampleCN: 一个硕大的身影堵住了门口。
senses.why: The same size metaphor now applies to a body: bulk that fills a space is read as terrain.
senses.whyCN: 同一个尺度比喻现在用到了身体上：占满空间的体量被读成地形。

intro.en: Mountainous is an English derivative of mountain plus the Latin suffix -ous. Its first recorded use is early modern, and the dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mountainous 是英语由 mountain 加拉丁后缀 -ous 构成的派生词，最早书证见于近代早期，年代为约数。

items.en: Latin -osus meant 'full of, abounding in', as in montuosus 'mountainous' and formosus 'shapely'.
items.cn: 拉丁 -osus 表示「充满、富于」，如 montuosus「多山的」与 formosus「形状美好的」。

items.en: Old French -ous, from Latin -osus, became the productive adjective ending that English borrowed with many Romance words.
items.cn: 古法语 -ous 来自拉丁 -osus，成为英语随大量罗曼语词借入的能产形容词词尾。

items.en: English already had mountaine as a noun; the adjective was formed on the English noun with the borrowed suffix rather than taken whole from Latin.
items.cn: 英语此时已有名词 mountaine；形容词是在英语名词上附加借来的后缀构成，而非整词借自拉丁语。

items.en: The written adjective is recorded from the sixteenth century, first describing terrain and later extending to huge waves and large amounts.
items.cn: 该形容词的书证见于 16 世纪，最初描写地形，后来扩展到巨浪与大量事物。

items.en: The senses 'huge in amount' and 'extremely difficult' are later figurative extensions built on the visible height of a mountain.
items.cn: 「数量庞大」与「极其艰巨」两个义项是后来的比喻延伸，建立在山可见的高度之上。

note.en: The first group holds words built on or beside mountain; the second holds adjectives for steep, high terrain.
note.cn: 第一组是与 mountain 同族或形近的词；第二组是表示陡峭高地的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun that mountainous is built on; it names the thing, while the adjective describes a place full of it.
entries.definitionCN: mountainous 所依附的名词；它指山本身，而形容词描述充满山的地区。

entries.definition: The adverb form, describing how something is shaped or how large it is; it is not a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，描述某物的形状或规模；并非另一个词根。

entries.definition: A technical adjective for the mountain zone of a region, built directly on Latin montanus; mountainous describes the whole area, montane names a belt.
entries.definitionCN: 直接由拉丁 montanus 构成的技术形容词，指某一地区的山地地带；mountainous 描述整片地区，montane 命名一条地带。

entries.definition: A person who climbs mountains; it shares the mountain stem but names an agent, not a landscape.
entries.definitionCN: 登山者；共享 mountain 词干，但指人，不指地貌。

entries.definition: Having many hills rather than mountains; the slopes are lower and rounder, so hilly is milder than mountainous.
entries.definitionCN: 有许多小丘而非高山；坡更低更圆，因此 hilly 比 mountainous 温和。

entries.definition: Belonging to the zone above the tree line, or to the Alps by name; it stresses altitude and ecology, not the mere presence of mountains.
entries.definitionCN: 指树线以上的高山区，或专指阿尔卑斯山；强调海拔与生态，而不只是有山。

entries.definition: Describing rough, uneven terrain; it stresses texture and difficulty of passage rather than height.
entries.definitionCN: 形容崎岖不平的地形；强调表面的粗糙与通行困难，而非高度。

entries.definition: Extremely tall, used of peaks, buildings or people; it describes height from the viewer's angle, not a whole region.
entries.definitionCN: 极高的，用于山峰、建筑或人；从观看者角度描述高度，不指整片地区。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real suffix -ous, the real base noun and the fixed phrases that separate terrain from metaphor.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的后缀 -ous、真实的基础名词，以及区分地形义与比喻义的固定搭配。

normal.en: mountain + -ous 'full of': a place full of mountains.
normal.cn: mountain + -ous「充满」：装满了山的地区。

normal.en: The suffix is Latin -osus, also seen in dangerous, famous and spacious.
normal.cn: 这个后缀是拉丁 -osus，也见于 dangerous、famous 与 spacious。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: mountainous region, mountainous terrain, mountainous waves.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 mountainous region、mountainous terrain、mountainous waves。

normal.en: The base noun keeps the concrete sense; the adjective can move to debt, tasks and bodies.
normal.cn: 基础名词保留具体义；形容词则可以移到债务、任务与身体上。

normal.en: Compare montane: mountainous describes the whole region, montane names the high belt inside it.
normal.cn: 对比 montane：mountainous 描述整片地区，montane 命名其中的高山地带。

abstract.en: Picture a map where flat green shrinks until almost every cell is brown ridge.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，平坦的绿色不断缩小，直到几乎每一格都是褐色的山脊。

abstract.en: Picture a wave photographed from a low boat so that it fills the frame like a cliff.
abstract.cn: 想象从低矮的小船上拍摄一道浪，它像悬崖一样占满画面。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of bills so high that it hides the person behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠账单高到把后面的人完全挡住。

examples.en: The mountainous border region is crossed by only two paved roads.
examples.cn: 这片多山的边境地区只有两条铺装公路穿过。

examples.en: Mountainous seas forced the ferry to stay in port.
examples.cn: 如山的海况迫使渡轮留在港内。

examples.en: The project became a mountainous effort once the old pipes were exposed.
examples.cn: 旧管道一暴露出来，这项工程就变成了一项艰巨的大工程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「毛（mao）+ 天（tain）+ 乐死（ous）」—— 毛茸茸的山顶顶到天，看得人乐坏了 → 多山的

root: mountain + -ous（拉丁 -osus「充满……的」）→ 字面「充满山的」；mountain 源自拉丁 mons、montis。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from a landscape full of peaks, then lend that height to waves, debts, objects, tasks, terrain classes and bodies.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「遍地是山的地区」出发，再把这种高度借给波浪、债务、物体、任务、地形类别与身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface with almost no flat ground left between ridge after ridge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片地面上，山脊一道接一道，几乎不剩平地。

branches.en: THE LAND ITSELF: ordinary description and technical terrain classification.
branches.cn: 土地本身：日常描述与技术性的地形分类。

branches.en: LIFE IN THAT LAND: climate, roads and villages take the label as their setting.
branches.cn: 那片土地上的生活：气候、道路与村庄把这个标签当作自身场景。

branches.en: HEIGHT WITHOUT ROCK: waves and icebergs borrow the profile of a peak.
branches.cn: 没有岩石的高度：巨浪与冰山借用山峰的轮廓。

branches.en: SCALE AS BURDEN: huge amounts and hard tasks become mountains you must move.
branches.cn: 规模即负担：庞大数量与艰难任务变成必须搬动的山。

branches.en: THE BODY AS TERRAIN: a bulk that fills a doorway is read like a slope.
branches.cn: 身体即地形：堵住门口的巨大体量被读成一面坡。

intro.en: The adjective is transparent: a native-borrowed noun plus a Latin suffix that means 'full of'.
intro.cn: 这个形容词的构造一目了然：一个借入的名词加上表示「充满」的拉丁后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin -osus produced Old French -ous, the ending English uses in numerous adjectives of abundance or character.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 -osus 产生古法语 -ous，英语用它构成大量表示「富于」或「具有某种性质」的形容词。

items.structure: Latin -osus via Old French -ous (full of, having)
items.meaning: full of; having the quality of
items.example: The suffix turns a noun into a descriptive adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成描述性形容词。

items.structure: Old French montaigne, from Latin mons, montis
items.meaning: a high raised mass of land
items.example: The mountain is visible from the coast.
items.exampleCN: 从海岸就能看见这座山。

items.example: The island is mountainous in the interior.
items.exampleCN: 这座岛的内陆是多山的。

items.example: The cliffs rise mountainously above the bay.
items.exampleCN: 悬崖如山地耸立在海湾之上。

items.example: The report measured the mountainousness of each district.
items.exampleCN: 报告测量了每个行政区的多山程度。

items.example: Montane species move uphill as the climate warms.
items.exampleCN: 随着气候变暖，山地物种向更高处迁移。

items.example: The mountaineer waited for a clear window.
items.exampleCN: 登山者在等一个晴朗的时间窗口。

items.example: Mountaineering grew popular in the nineteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 登山运动在 19 世纪流行起来。

items.example: The range runs north for three hundred kilometres.
items.exampleCN: 这条山脉向北延伸三百公里。

latinEntries.meaning: of or belonging to a mountain

definition_zh: 山脉；山系；连绵的山体带
definition_en: a long connected line of mountains, or the whole system of folded rock that produced it
core_image: 许多山峰沿同一条线排开，峰与峰之间由鞍部相连，远看像一道起伏的长墙
scene: 西边的地平线上，一道接一道的山脊连成不断的长线。A mountain range runs along the whole western border.
sceneCN: 此处指「由多座山体相连而成的一长列山脉」（第 1 个义项：山峰沿同一方向连续排列）；句意为一条山脉沿整条西部边界延伸。图中可辨识物件：地平线、连续的山脊、山与山之间的鞍部、远处泛蓝的轮廓。

pos.zh: 山脉；山系（可数，复数 mountain ranges）

collocations.phrase: the crest of the mountain range

derivatives.zh: 一列；范围 / 排列；延伸

senses.title: A connected line of mountains
senses.definition: a series of mountains connected by high ground and extending in one direction
senses.definitionCN: 由高地相连、沿同一方向延伸的一系列山体
senses.example: The Andes form the longest mountain range on land.
senses.exampleCN: 安第斯山脉是陆地上最长的山脉。
senses.why: Range first meant a row or line; a mountain range is simply mountains arranged in that row.
senses.whyCN: 短语的第二部分最初意为「一排、一列」；整个短语就是把山排成那样的一列。

senses.title: A single folded rock system
senses.titleCN: 山系：同一次造山运动的整体
senses.definition: the whole geological structure produced by one episode of mountain building
senses.definitionCN: 由同一次造山运动产生的整套地质构造
senses.example: Geologists treat the range as one folded system.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家把这条山脉视为一个褶皱系统。
senses.why: Geology shifts from the visible line of peaks to the deep structure that holds them together.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把视线从可见的峰线移到把这些峰连在一起的深部构造上。

senses.title: The highland region it occupies
senses.definition: the mountainous country that a range fills, including its valleys and slopes
senses.definitionCN: 一条山脉所占据的山地地带，包括谷地与坡面
senses.example: Farms in the range depend on snowmelt in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这片山脉里的农场依靠春季融雪。
senses.why: A line on a map is also a place where people live, so the name of the line comes to mean the region.
senses.whyCN: 地图上的一条线也是人们生活的地方，于是这条线的名字转指整片地区。

senses.title: Its direction of extension
senses.definition: the direction in which the connected peaks continue across the land
senses.definitionCN: 相连山峰在地面上继续延伸的方向
senses.example: The range bends north near the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山脉在海岸附近转向北方。
senses.why: Because range means a line, the word can name the path of the line as well as the things on it.
senses.whyCN: 因为第二部分的本义是线，整个短语既能指线上的物体，也能指这条线本身的路径。

senses.title: A natural barrier
senses.definition: a range viewed as a wall that hinders travel, wind or invasion
senses.definitionCN: 被视作阻碍通行、风或入侵的一道墙的山脉
senses.example: The range sheltered the valley from the worst of the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山脉为山谷挡住了风暴最猛的部分。
senses.why: Anything long, high and continuous works as a wall; the word for the line becomes the word for the obstacle.
senses.whyCN: 凡是长、高、连续的东西都能当墙用；指「线」的词于是变成指「障碍」的词。

senses.title: A climate divide
senses.definition: a range that separates a wet windward side from a dry leeward side
senses.definitionCN: 把湿润的迎风面与干燥的背风面分开的山脉
senses.example: The range divides the wet coast from the dry interior.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山脉把湿润的海岸与干燥的内陆分开。
senses.why: A barrier that blocks air also sorts climates, so the same line becomes a boundary between weather zones.
senses.whyCN: 挡住空气的屏障也把气候分了类，同一条线于是成为天气带之间的边界。

senses.title: A belt of mineral or forest wealth
senses.definition: a range considered as the zone that carries ore, timber or water resources
senses.definitionCN: 被视作承载矿藏、林木或水资源的带状山脉
senses.example: The range holds most of the region's copper.
senses.exampleCN: 这一地区的大部分铜矿都在这条山脉里。
senses.why: Resources follow rock, and rock follows the line, so the line becomes an economic unit.
senses.whyCN: 资源跟着岩层走，岩层跟着这条线走，这条线于是成了一个经济单位。

senses.title: Its silhouette on the horizon
senses.titleCN: 远望时的连绵天际轮廓
senses.definition: the visible outline of connected peaks seen from a distance
senses.definitionCN: 从远处看到的相连山峰的可见轮廓
senses.example: At dusk the range turns blue against the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时，这条山脉在天边变成一片蓝色。
senses.why: From far away only the outline survives; the range becomes a single drawn shape rather than many separate peaks.
senses.whyCN: 从远处看，只剩轮廓还在；整条山脉变成一个画出来的形状，而不是许多分开的峰。

intro.en: Mountain range joins a Latin-derived noun with a word for a row or line that came through Old French from a Germanic stem. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mountain range 由拉丁来源的名词与一个表示「排、列」的词组合而成；后者经古法语来自日耳曼语词干，年代均为约数。

items.en: The mountain part goes back to Latin mons, montis 'mountain' and its adjective montanus 'of a mountain'; the deeper Indo-European origin is unsettled.
items.cn: mountain 这一部分上溯至拉丁 mons、montis「山」及其形容词 montanus「山的」；更早的印欧来源尚无定论。

items.en: Old French montagne, from Vulgar Latin *montanea 'mountainous country', supplied the English noun in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 montagne 来自通俗拉丁语 *montanea「多山地带」，在 14 世纪为英语提供了这个名词。

items.en: Range traces to Old French rang 'row, line', generally derived from Frankish *hring 'ring, circle', a reconstructed form; the same Germanic word also gave English ring.
items.cn: range 上溯至古法语 rang「排、列」，一般认为来自法兰克语 *hring「环、圈」，这是重构形式；同一个日耳曼词也给出了英语 ring。

items.en: The verb rangier 'to place in rows' produced both the English noun range and the verb to range, so the row and the act of arranging share one source.
items.cn: 动词 rangier「排成行」同时产生了英语名词 range 与动词 range，因此「行列」与「排列的动作」同出一源。

items.en: The fixed phrase mountain range is recorded from the eighteenth century, when travellers and geographers needed a name for a whole connected series rather than a single peak.
items.cn: mountain range 这一固定短语见于 18 世纪，当时旅行者与地理学家需要一个词来指整条相连的山列，而不是单独一座峰。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and root of the first element): no exact first citation for the compound is agreed, and the pre-Latin origin of mons remains a reconstruction; the Frankish form is likewise reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与前一成分的词根）：该复合词没有公认的最早书证；mons 在拉丁语之前的来源仍属重构，法兰克语形式同样属重构。

note.en: The first group holds words that look like mountain range or share one of its parts; the second holds technical names for connected uplands.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或共享其中一个成分的词；第二组是表示相连高地的技术名称。

entries.definition: A row, a extent or a field of activity; by itself it does not mean mountains, so mountain range adds the material.
entries.definitionCN: 指一排、一段范围或一个活动领域；单独使用时不指山，因此 mountain range 要补出材质。

entries.definition: A single high mass of land; a range is what you get when many of them line up.
entries.definitionCN: 单座高耸的陆地块体；许多座排成一线，才成为山脉。

entries.definition: To climb or get on, or a word used before names such as Mount Kenya; it is not the compound noun.
entries.definitionCN: 表示登上、骑上，或用于 Mount Kenya 一类专名之前；它不是这个复合名词。

entries.definition: To put things in order; it comes from the same Old French rangier family as range, but it has no mountain sense.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物排好；与 range 同出古法语 rangier 词族，但没有山的意义。

entries.definition: A series of connected mountains; chain stresses the links between the masses, while range stresses the line they form.
entries.definitionCN: 相连的一系列山体；chain 强调山块之间的连接，range 强调它们排成的线。

entries.definition: A long system of parallel ranges, borrowed from Spanish; it is used in geography for the largest scale.
entries.definitionCN: 由多条平行山脉组成的巨大山系，借自西班牙语；地理学用它指最大尺度。

entries.definition: A compact group of mountains that stands as one block; it is not long and linear like a range.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一个整体块体矗立的紧凑山群；不像山脉那样长而呈线状。

entries.definition: A range with a jagged saw-like crest, from Spanish sierra 'saw'; it names a profile, not just a line.
entries.definitionCN: 山脊呈锯齿状的一条山脉，来自西班牙语 sierra「锯」；它命名一种轮廓，而不只是线。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real row sense of range, the real compound and the technical synonyms geographers use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：range 真实的「排、列」义、真实的复合方式，以及地理学家使用的技术同义词。

normal.en: range = a row; mountain range = mountains in a row.
normal.cn: range = 一排；mountain range = 排成一排的山。

normal.en: Range and arrange share Old French rangier 'to put in rows'.
normal.cn: range 与 arrange 共享古法语 rangier「排成行」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: a long mountain range, the crest of the mountain range, cross the mountain range.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 a long mountain range、the crest of the mountain range、cross the mountain range。

normal.en: Technical synonyms split by shape: chain for links, massif for a block, sierra for a saw-toothed crest.
normal.cn: 技术同义词按形状分工：chain 强调连接，massif 强调整块，sierra 强调锯齿状脊线。

normal.en: The range is also a barrier, a climate divide and a resource belt, because a long wall does all three jobs.
normal.cn: 山脉同时是屏障、气候分界与资源带，因为一道长墙能兼做这三件事。

abstract.en: Picture a row of tents pitched along one path, each touching the next.
abstract.cn: 想象沿同一条小路搭起一排帐篷，每一顶都挨着下一顶。

abstract.en: Picture a single thread pulled through many beads so that the beads become one line.
abstract.cn: 想象一根线穿过许多珠子，珠子于是连成一条线。

abstract.en: Picture a wall long enough that changing weather on one side never reaches the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙长到一边的天气变化永远到不了另一边。

examples.en: The Rocky Mountains form a mountain range that runs from Canada to New Mexico.
examples.cn: 落基山脉构成一条从加拿大延伸到新墨西哥的山脉。

examples.en: Rain falls heavily on the coastal side of the mountain range.
examples.cn: 降雨大量落在山脉靠海的一侧。

examples.en: Roads through the mountain range are often closed in winter.
examples.cn: 穿越这条山脉的公路在冬季常被封闭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「山（mountain）+ 排（range）」—— 山排成一长排 → 山脉

root: mountain（拉丁 mons、montis「山」）+ range（古法语 rang「排、列」，一般认为源自法兰克语 *hring「环」，属重构形式）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all begin with the same picture of peaks in a row, then read that row as a structure, a region, a direction, a wall, a climate border, a resource belt and a silhouette.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从「山峰排成一列」这幅图出发，再把这一列读成构造、地区、走向、墙、气候边界、资源带与轮廓。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many peaks threaded onto one line, like beads on a string.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多山峰穿在同一根线上，像串起的珠子。

branches.en: THE LINE ITSELF: what is seen first is the row, then the direction in which the row continues.
branches.cn: 线本身：最先看到的是这一排，然后是这一排继续延伸的方向。

branches.en: THE DEEP STRUCTURE: the visible row is the surface of one folded rock system.
branches.cn: 深部构造：可见的一排只是同一个褶皱岩系的表面。

branches.en: THE WHOLE TERRITORY: the line becomes a place to live in and a belt of resources.
branches.cn: 整片地域：这条线变成可居住的地方，也变成一条资源带。

branches.en: THE WALL: continuity makes the range block travel, wind and weather.
branches.cn: 墙：连续性使山脉挡住通行、风与天气。

branches.en: THE OUTLINE: from far away only the drawn edge of the row remains.
branches.cn: 轮廓：从远处看，只剩这一排画出的边缘。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two ordinary words; its technical force comes from geography, which fixed the combination.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个普通词构成；它的技术含义来自地理学，是地理学固定了这一组合。

latinIntro.en: Only the mountain element has a Latin etymon (mons, montis). Range has no Latin root: it comes through Old French from a reconstructed Frankish form, so the Latin list covers the first element only.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 mountain 这一成分有拉丁词源（mons、montis）。range 没有拉丁词根：它经古法语来自一个重构的法兰克语形式，因此拉丁条目只覆盖前一个成分。

items.structure: Old French montaigne, from Latin mons, montis
items.meaning: a high raised mass of land
items.example: The mountain is older than the range.
items.exampleCN: 这座山比整条山脉更古老。

items.meaning: a row or line; to arrange in a line
items.example: The peaks stand in a long range.
items.exampleCN: 这些山峰排成长长的一列。

items.example: The mountain range runs north.

items.example: The chain continues under the sea.

items.meaning: a band of mountains across a region
items.example: A narrow mountain belt separates the basins.

items.meaning: the geological whole formed by related ranges
items.meaningCN: 由相关山脉构成的地质整体

items.meaning: a long system of parallel ranges
items.meaningCN: 由多条平行山脉组成的长大山系
items.example: The cordillera feeds rivers on both sides.

definition_zh: 山峰；顶点；峰值；帽檐；达到最高点
definition_en: the pointed top of a mountain; the highest point or maximum of anything; the front edge of a cap; to reach a maximum
core_image: 一条上升的线越来越陡，最后收成一个尖，然后开始下落
scene: 登山队在最后一段岩壁上放慢脚步，前方只剩一小块尖顶。Only a narrow peak remained above the last stretch of rock.
sceneCN: 此处指「山体最上端的尖顶」（第 1 个义项：山脊收束成的最高尖点）；句意为最后一段岩壁之上只剩一个狭窄的尖顶。图中可辨识物件：岩壁、狭窄的尖顶、登山绳、放慢脚步的队员。

pos.zh: 山峰；山顶；最高点；峰值；帽檐；尖端
达到最高点；达到峰值
高峰的；峰值的（作定语，如 peak hours）

senses.title: The pointed top of a mountain
senses.definition: the sharp upper end of a mountain, where its slopes meet
senses.definitionCN: 山体最上端的尖点，坡面在此交会
senses.example: Only a narrow peak remained above the last stretch of rock.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一段岩壁之上只剩一个狭窄的尖顶。
senses.why: The earliest sense is a pointed top: the word names the shape where two slopes finally meet.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项是「尖顶」：这个词命名两条坡面最终相交的那个形状。

senses.title: The highest point of a climb
senses.definition: the top that a climber reaches after ascending a mountain
senses.definitionCN: 攀登者上到山顶后所抵达的最高处
senses.example: They reached the peak just before the clouds closed in.
senses.exampleCN: 他们赶在云雾合拢之前登上了顶峰。
senses.why: A climb ends at the highest point, so the top became the goal of the whole action.
senses.whyCN: 攀登在最高点结束，于是这个顶端成了整个动作的目标。

senses.title: The high point of a career or period
senses.definition: the moment of greatest success or intensity in a process
senses.definitionCN: 一个过程中最成功或最强烈的时刻
senses.example: Her career reached its peak in the early nineties.
senses.exampleCN: 她的事业在九十年代初达到顶峰。
senses.why: A curve that rises and falls gives the metaphor: the best moment is the point where the line stops climbing.
senses.whyCN: 先升后落的曲线提供了比喻：最好的时刻就是那条线停止上升的那一点。

senses.title: A maximum value in data
senses.definition: the highest value recorded in a series, graph or measurement
senses.definitionCN: 在一组数据、图表或测量中记录到的最高值
senses.example: The graph shows a sharp peak around noon.
senses.exampleCN: 图表显示中午前后有一个陡峭的峰值。
senses.why: Statistics keeps the geometry literal: the maximum is drawn as the top of a curve.
senses.whyCN: 统计学保留了字面的几何形状：最大值被画成曲线的顶端。

senses.title: The busiest period
senses.definition: the time when traffic, demand or activity is greatest
senses.definitionCN: 交通、需求或活动最旺盛的时段
senses.example: Trains are crowded during peak hours.
senses.exampleCN: 高峰时段火车很拥挤。
senses.why: If activity is a curve, the busiest hour is where the curve peaks; the noun then names that hour.
senses.whyCN: 如果活动是一条曲线，最忙的那一小时就是曲线到达顶点之处；名词随后就指那个小时。

senses.title: The front edge of a cap
senses.definition: the projecting front part of a cap that shades the eyes
senses.definitionCN: 帽子前方突出、用来遮住眼睛的部分
senses.example: He pulled his cap down by the peak.
senses.exampleCN: 他抓住帽檐把帽子往下拉。
senses.why: A cap's brim projects forward and comes to a point, so the same shape word applies to clothing.
senses.whyCN: 帽檐向前突出并收成一个尖，同一个形状词于是也用于衣物。

senses.title: A projecting tip of anything
senses.titleCN: 任何物体的尖端或突出部
senses.definition: the pointed projecting part of a roof, beard or other object
senses.definitionCN: 屋顶、胡须或其他物体尖而突出的部分
senses.example: Rain ran off the peak of the tent.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水从帐篷的尖顶流下。
senses.why: The shape, not the mountain, is the core: any surface that rises to a point has a peak.
senses.whyCN: 核心是形状而不是山：任何升到一点的表面都有这样一个尖顶。

senses.title: To reach a maximum
senses.definition: to rise to the highest level and then stop rising
senses.definitionCN: 上升到最高水平后不再上升
senses.example: Sales peaked in December and fell sharply afterwards.
senses.exampleCN: 销量在十二月见顶，随后急剧下降。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: something peaks when it reaches the top of its own curve.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：某物到达自身曲线的顶端，就是「见顶」。

intro.en: Peak is a northern English word of uncertain Germanic origin; the mountain sense and the figurative senses developed in later centuries. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: peak 是一个来源不确定的英格兰北部词，属日耳曼语系；山的义项与比喻义是后来几个世纪发展出来的，年代均为约数。

items.en: Middle English pek, recorded in the fourteenth century, meant 'a pointed top or projecting point', not specifically a mountain.
items.cn: 中古英语 pek 见于 14 世纪，意为「尖顶或突出的尖端」，并不专指山。

items.en: The form is probably related to Old English pēac 'pinnacle' and to a reconstructed *pēc 'pointed hill'; both are uncertain and the exact link is disputed.
items.cn: 这一形式可能与古英语 pēac「尖塔、尖顶」以及重构形式 *pēc「尖山」有关；两者都不确定，具体关联仍有争议。

items.en: Similar words appear in Middle Low German and Dutch, which supports a Germanic origin, though no single source form can be pointed to with confidence.
items.cn: 中古低地德语与荷兰语中有相似词，这支持日耳曼语来源，但无法有把握地指出某一个唯一的来源形式。

items.en: The specific sense 'pointed top of a mountain' is recorded in the sixteenth century, and 'the highest point of a mountain' became standard in the eighteenth.
items.cn: 「山峰的尖顶」这一具体义项见于 16 世纪，而「山的最高点」在 18 世纪成为通行用法。

items.en: From the late eighteenth century peak was used for the highest point of anything, including careers and graphs; the transport sense 'peak hours' belongs to the twentieth century.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪晚期起，peak 用于任何事物的最高点，包括事业与图表；交通义「高峰时段」则属于 20 世纪。

items.en: Source uncertain (root and first date): the pre-Germanic origin is unknown, the Old English connection is a hypothesis, and the earliest citations are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：日耳曼语之前的来源不明，与古英语的关联只是假说，最早书证年代为约数。

note.en: The first group is made of exact or near homophones that are constantly confused in writing; the second holds words for the top of something.
note.cn: 第一组是书写中极易混淆的同音或近音词；第二组是表示「某物顶端」的词。

entries.definition: To look quickly or secretly; the spelling with double e marks the glance, not the summit.
entries.definitionCN: 快速地或偷偷地看一眼；双 e 的拼写标记「瞥一眼」，与山顶无关。

entries.definition: To annoy someone, or to stimulate interest; it comes from French piquer 'to prick', a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 激怒某人，或激起兴趣；来自法语 piquer「刺」，词根不同。

entries.definition: The past tense of the verb or an adjective meaning 'having a peak'; as an adjective it can also mean pale and ill-looking.
entries.definitionCN: 动词过去式，或表示「有尖顶的」形容词；作形容词时还可指面色苍白、有病容。

entries.definition: A bird's bill; the vowel is the same but the first consonant is /b/, not /p/.
entries.definitionCN: 鸟喙；元音相同，但首辅音是 /b/ 而非 /p/。

entries.definition: The highest point of a mountain, used especially of reaching it and of top-level meetings; it is more formal than peak.
entries.definitionCN: 山的最高点，尤用于「登顶」与首脑会议；比 peak 更正式。

entries.definition: The highest point of a shape or system, used in geometry and formal writing; it is a Latin loan and does not name a mountain by itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形状或系统的最高点，用于几何与正式写作；它是拉丁借词，本身不指山。

entries.definition: The top line of a ridge or wave rather than a single point; a crest can be long, a peak is sharp.
entries.definitionCN: 山脊或波浪的顶线，而不是一个点；crest 可以是长的，peak 是尖的。

entries.definition: The highest part of anything, in everyday speech; it lacks the sharp, pointed image that peak carries.
entries.definitionCN: 日常语中任何事物的最高部分；它没有 peak 那种尖锐的意象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real spelling contrasts with peek and pique, and the real phrases that mark the senses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：与 peek、pique 的真实拼写对比，以及标记各义项的真实搭配。

normal.en: peak (mountain) vs peek (glance) vs pique (prick of annoyance): three spellings, one sound.
normal.cn: peak（山）对 peek（瞥）对 pique（被刺恼）：三个拼写，一个读音。

normal.en: The shape is a curve: rise, top, fall — the top is the peak.
normal.cn: 形状是一条曲线：上升、到顶、下落——顶端就是 peak。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: reach the peak, peak hours, peak season, at its peak.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 reach the peak、peak hours、peak season、at its peak。

normal.en: A cap has a peak, and so does a tent; anything pointed upward qualifies.
normal.cn: 帽子有帽檐，帐篷也有尖顶；凡是向上收成尖的东西都算。

normal.en: As a verb it only means 'reach the maximum', never 'climb a mountain'.
normal.cn: 作动词时只表示「达到最大值」，从不表示「爬山」。

abstract.en: Picture a fever chart that climbs all night and turns over at dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象一张体温曲线整夜攀升，在黎明时翻转而下。

abstract.en: Picture a wave that holds its highest drop for one second before breaking.
abstract.cn: 想象一道浪在崩碎前把最高的水滴保持一秒钟。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd that fills a station at eight and is gone by nine.
abstract.cn: 想象人群在八点塞满车站，到九点又散尽。

examples.en: The peak was hidden by cloud for most of the afternoon.
examples.cn: 整个下午大部分时间，山峰都被云遮着。

examples.en: Demand for electricity peaks on the coldest evenings.
examples.cn: 最冷的傍晚用电需求达到峰值。

examples.en: Avoid the peak hours if you are driving to the airport.
examples.cn: 如果开车去机场，避开高峰时段。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「劈（pi）+ 克（k）」—— 一刀劈下去，山顶被削成一个尖 → 山峰；顶点

root: 中古英语 pek「尖顶」，可能上溯至古英语 pēac「尖塔」或重构的 *pēc「尖山」，属日耳曼语系；更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all rest on one shape: a line rises to a single sharp top, whether that line is rock, a career, a graph, a timetable, a cap or a tent.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都立在一个形状上：一条线升到一个尖顶，无论这条线是岩石、事业、图表、时刻表、帽子还是帐篷。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rising line that steepens into a point and then turns down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条上升的线越来越陡，收成一点，然后向下转折。

branches.en: SHAPE: any surface that ends in a point has a peak, from rock to canvas.
branches.cn: 形状：凡是收成一点的表面都有尖端，从岩石到帆布都算。

branches.en: GOAL: the top is what the climb aims at.
branches.cn: 目标：顶端就是攀登所指向的东西。

branches.en: CURVE: the best moment and the highest number are both the top of a line.
branches.cn: 曲线：最好的时刻与最高的数值都是某条线的顶端。

branches.en: TIME: the busiest hour is the hour when activity is at its top.
branches.cn: 时间：最忙的那一小时，就是活动到达顶端的那一小时。

branches.en: EDGE AND ACTION: a cap's brim is a forward point, and to peak is to reach the top.
branches.cn: 边缘与动作：帽檐是向前的尖，而 peak 作动词就是到达顶端。

intro.en: Peak is a bare Germanic stem with only a few English extensions; most of its family is compounds rather than suffixes.
intro.cn: peak 是一个光秃的日耳曼语词干，英语派生有限；它的词族多为复合词而非后缀派生。

latinIntro.en: No Latin etymon is recoverable: peak goes back to an uncertain Germanic form, so the Latin entry list is empty by design.
latinIntro.cn: 无法追溯到拉丁词源：peak 上溯至一个不确定的日耳曼语形式，因此拉丁条目按规则留空。

definition_zh: 山顶；最高点；登顶；峰会；最高层
definition_en: the highest point of a mountain; the act of reaching it; a meeting of top leaders; the highest level of anything
core_image: 山坡四面收拢，最后留出一小块最高的平台，站在上面可以看见所有方向

sceneCN: 此处指「山体最高的那一小块平台」（第 1 个义项：四面坡面收拢而成的最高处）；句意为天亮时他们站在山顶，看影子移动。图中可辨识物件：平坦雪面、四周下落的坡、移动的山影、队员的冰镐。

最高级别的（如 summit meeting、summit talks）

senses.title: The highest point of a mountain
senses.definition: the top surface or highest point of a mountain
senses.definitionCN: 山体最上端的表面或最高点
senses.example: At dawn they stood on the summit and watched the shadow move.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮时他们站在山顶，看着影子移动。
senses.why: Latin summus meant 'highest', so summit names the topmost part rather than the whole mountain.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 summus 意为「最高的」，所以这个词指最上面的部分，而不是整座山。

senses.title: The act or goal of reaching the top
senses.definition: the achievement of climbing to the top of a mountain
senses.definitionCN: 爬上山顶这一成就
senses.example: The team made the summit after eleven hours of climbing.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍攀登十一个小时后登顶。
senses.why: The place stands for the action: to make the summit is to complete the climb that ends there.
senses.whyCN: 地点代指动作：登上该处，就是完成以它为终点的攀登。

senses.title: A meeting of top leaders
senses.definition: a meeting between heads of government or top officials
senses.definitionCN: 政府首脑或最高官员之间的会议
senses.example: The two leaders will meet at a summit next month.
senses.exampleCN: 两位领导人下个月将在一次峰会上会面。
senses.why: Politics borrowed the mountain image: the people at the top of their governments meet at a 'top' of their own.
senses.whyCN: 政治借用了山的意象：站在各自政府顶端的人，在属于他们的「顶端」会面。

senses.title: The highest point of a career
senses.definition: the most successful or highest stage of a person's life or work
senses.definitionCN: 一个人生活或工作中最成功、最高的阶段
senses.example: Winning the prize marked the summit of her career.
senses.exampleCN: 获奖标志着她事业的顶点。
senses.why: A career is imagined as a climb, so its best stage is the top of the slope.
senses.whyCN: 事业被想象成一次攀登，因此它最好的阶段就是坡面的顶端。

senses.title: The top level of a hierarchy
senses.definition: the highest rank or level within an organisation or system
senses.definitionCN: 一个组织或体系中最高的等级或层次
senses.example: The decision was taken at the summit of the organisation.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定是在该组织的最高层做出的。
senses.why: Rank is drawn as height: the fewer people above you, the closer you are to the summit.
senses.whyCN: 等级被画成高度：上面的人越少，你离顶端越近。

senses.title: The maximum of a curve
senses.definition: the highest value or turning point of a measured curve
senses.definitionCN: 一条测量曲线上的最高值或转折点
senses.example: The curve reaches its summit in midsummer.
senses.exampleCN: 这条曲线在仲夏达到最高点。
senses.why: Mathematics keeps the spatial image: the maximum is literally the top of the drawn line.
senses.whyCN: 数学保留了空间意象：最大值就是画出的那条线字面上的顶端。

senses.title: Attributive: top-level
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean the highest-level version of a meeting or event
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，表示会议或活动的最高级别形式
senses.example: Summit talks resumed after a three-year pause.
senses.exampleCN: 最高级别会谈在中断三年后恢复。
senses.why: The noun simply labels the rank of the event that follows it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词只是给它后面的活动标出等级。

senses.title: The flat top surface you can stand on
senses.definition: the small area at the very top of a mountain, wide enough for people or a hut
senses.definitionCN: 山顶上可以容人或容小屋的一小块面积
senses.example: The summit is wide enough for a small weather station.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山顶宽到可以放一座小型气象站。
senses.why: A point in geometry is not a place to stand; the word also names the usable top surface.
senses.whyCN: 几何上的点不能站人；这个词也指那块可用的顶面。

intro.en: Summit came from Old French and goes back to Latin summus 'highest'. The diplomatic sense is recent, and dates are approximate.
intro.cn: summit 来自古法语，上溯至拉丁 summus「最高的」。外交义是晚近发展，年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin summus, superlative of superus 'upper', meant 'highest, topmost'; the neuter summum named the top or the highest point.
items.cn: 拉丁 summus 是 superus「上方的」的最高级，意为「最高的、最上的」；中性形式 summum 指顶端或最高点。

items.en: The comparative root is super 'above, over', from an Indo-European form also seen in English over and hyper-.
items.cn: 比较级词根是 super「在上、超过」，其印欧形式也见于英语 over 与 hyper-。

items.en: Old French formed the diminutive somete, later sommet, 'a small top', which narrowed the meaning to the top of a hill or mountain.
items.cn: 古法语构成指小形式 somete（后来作 sommet），意为「小顶端」，把意义收窄到小山或山的顶。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the fifteenth century; the spelling summit reflects the Latin stem rather than the French form.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪借入这个词；拼写 summit 反映的是拉丁词干，而不是法语形式。

items.en: The use for a meeting of heads of government is recorded from the mid-twentieth century, first in journalism about Cold War talks.
items.cn: 用于政府首脑会议这一义项见于 20 世纪中期，最早出现在关于冷战会谈的新闻报道中。

items.en: The root and the main line are secure; only the first date is uncertain. No part of the etymology beyond Latin super is established, so any deeper Indo-European form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 词根与主要线索是可靠的，只有首见年代不确定。拉丁 super 之后的更深来源均未确立，凡给出的更深印欧形式都属重构。

note.en: The first group holds words that look close to summit on the page; the second holds synonyms for the top of a mountain.
note.cn: 第一组是书面上与 summit 相近的词；第二组是表示山顶的同义词。

entries.definition: To yield or to send in a document; from sub- 'under' plus mittere 'send', so it is not a relative of summit.
entries.definitionCN: 屈服，或提交文件；来自 sub-「在下」加 mittere「送」，与 summit 并非同族。

entries.definition: To call someone to appear; from Latin summonere, sub- plus monere 'warn', unrelated to summus.
entries.definitionCN: 召唤某人到场；来自拉丁 summonere，即 sub- 加 monere「警告」，与 summus 无关。

entries.definition: A short account of the main points; it comes from Latin summarium, from summa 'total', a different branch of the same super- family.
entries.definitionCN: 对要点的简短陈述；来自拉丁 summarium，源于 summa「总数」，是同属 super- 词族的另一分支。

entries.definition: The practice of holding summits; it is summit plus -ry, so it is a derivative, not a look-alike.
entries.definitionCN: 举行峰会的做法；由 summit 加 -ry 构成，属派生词而非形近词。

entries.definition: The pointed top of a mountain; it is more everyday and more pointed, while summit is formal and often includes the top surface.
entries.definitionCN: 山的尖顶；更日常也更尖，而 summit 更正式，且常包含顶面。

entries.definition: The highest point of a shape or system; it is technical and rarely used for a real mountain.
entries.definitionCN: 形状或系统的最高点；属技术用语，很少用于真实的山。

entries.definition: The upper line of a ridge or wave; it is a line rather than a point, so it suits long ridges.
entries.definitionCN: 山脊或波浪的顶线；它是一条线而非一个点，适合长长的山脊。

entries.definition: A high pointed rock or the highest ornament of a building; it suggests a needle rather than a broad top.
entries.definitionCN: 高而尖的岩石或建筑顶端的装饰；暗示针状而非宽阔的顶面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin superlative, the real political metaphor and the fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁最高级、真实的政治比喻与固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin summus 'highest' is the superlative of superus 'upper'.
normal.cn: 拉丁 summus「最高的」是 superus「上方的」的最高级。

normal.en: The family runs summit, summitry, summiteer, summit meeting.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 summit、summitry、summiteer、summit meeting。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: reach the summit, summit talks, at the summit.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 reach the summit、summit talks、at the summit。

normal.en: The same top image gives the political sense: leaders meet at the top of their governments.
normal.cn: 同一个「顶端」意象给出政治义：领导人在各自政府的顶端会面。

normal.en: Summit suggests a place with room to stand; peak suggests a sharp point.
normal.cn: summit 暗示有地方可以站；peak 暗示尖锐的点。

abstract.en: Picture a cone cut flat at the very top so a person can stand there.
abstract.cn: 想象一个圆锥在最顶端被削平，容得下一个人站立。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder whose last step is a small platform above the clouds.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子，最后一级是云上一小块平台。

abstract.en: Picture a chart where the line stops climbing at exactly one point.
abstract.cn: 想象一张图表，那条线恰好在某一点停止上升。

examples.en: Snow on the summit never melts completely.
examples.cn: 山顶的雪从不完全融化。

examples.en: The summit ended without a joint statement.
examples.cn: 这次峰会结束时没有发表联合声明。

examples.en: He was at the summit of his powers when the illness struck.
examples.cn: 疾病袭来时，他正处于能力的顶峰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「撒（sa）+ 米（mi）+ 特（t）」—— 把米撒到最高的那一小块平台上 → 山顶；顶点

root: 拉丁 summus「最高的」（superus「上方的」的最高级）→ 古法语 somete/sommet「小顶端」→ 英语 summit。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all place something at the very top: a mountain, a climb, a meeting, a career, a hierarchy, a curve, an event's rank and a standable surface.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某物放在最顶端：一座山、一次攀登、一次会议、一段事业、一个层级、一条曲线、一项活动的等级，以及一块可站立的顶面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: slopes converge on one highest platform where every direction falls away.
core.cn: 核心意象：四面坡面汇到一块最高的平台，从那里每个方向都向下落。

branches.en: THE PLACE: the highest point and the small flat area that makes it usable.
branches.cn: 地点：最高点，以及使它可用的那一小块平地。

branches.en: THE ACHIEVEMENT: reaching the place completes the climb.
branches.cn: 成就：抵达该处就完成了攀登。

branches.en: THE CURVE: a career and a graph both stop rising at their summit.
branches.cn: 曲线：事业与图表都在各自的顶点停止上升。

branches.en: THE HIERARCHY: rank is height, and the highest level labels its meetings.
branches.cn: 层级：等级就是高度，最高层给它的会议贴上标签。

branches.en: THE POLITICAL METAPHOR: leaders meet at a summit of their own.
branches.cn: 政治比喻：领导人在属于他们自己的「顶端」会面。

intro.en: Summit is a Latin superlative routed through French, and English built a small political family on it in the twentieth century.
intro.cn: summit 是经法语传入的拉丁最高级形式，英语在 20 世纪围绕它造出一个小型政治词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin summus and summum belong to the super- family, with super 'above' and superus 'upper'; the Romance forms passed through Old French before reaching English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 summus 与 summum 属于 super- 词族，连同 super「在上」与 superus「上方的」；罗曼语形式经古法语才进入英语。

items.example: The stem summ- carries the idea of the top.
items.exampleCN: 词干 summ- 带着「顶端」的意思。

items.structure: Old French sommet, from Latin summum
items.example: The summit is above the clouds.
items.exampleCN: 山顶在云层之上。

items.example: Two summits face each other across the pass.
items.exampleCN: 两个山顶隔着山口相对。

items.meaning: the practice of holding summit meetings
items.example: Summitry became a regular habit after the war.
items.exampleCN: 战后峰会外交成了常规做法。

items.example: The summiteers arrived by separate planes.
items.exampleCN: 参加峰会的领导人分乘不同飞机抵达。

items.example: The summit meeting lasted two days.
items.exampleCN: 这次首脑会议持续了两天。

items.example: Summit talks resumed in spring.
items.exampleCN: 最高级别会谈在春季恢复。

items.meaning: the highest level of an organisation
items.example: The report went straight to summit level.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告直接送到了最高层。

definition_zh: 山脊；屋脊；长条形隆起；高压脊；田垄
definition_en: a long narrow raised top between two slopes; also the top line of a roof, a narrow bank, or a high-pressure band in weather maps
core_image: 两侧坡面向下退去，中间留出一条又窄又长的脊背，像动物的背线
scene: 雨水在两侧坡面汇成细流，中间那条窄长的脊背始终没有被冲开。We followed the ridge for three hours without losing the path.
sceneCN: 此处指「两侧坡面之间那条窄长的最高处」（第 1 个义项：山体分水的高脊线）；句意为他们沿着这条山脊走了三小时，一直没有偏离路径。图中可辨识物件：两侧坡面、汇流的雨水、窄长脊背、踩出的路径。

pos.zh: 山脊；脊线；屋脊；长条形隆起；高压脊；田垄
使成脊状；给……装屋脊；在……上起垄

senses.title: A long narrow mountain top
senses.definition: a long narrow raised top with slopes falling away on both sides
senses.definitionCN: 两侧坡面下落的狭长最高处
senses.example: We followed the ridge for three hours without losing the path.
senses.exampleCN: 我们沿着山脊走了三小时，没有偏离路径。
senses.why: The word first named an animal's back: a long raised line with two sides falling away. Mountains reuse the shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指动物的背：一条长隆起，两侧向下落。山沿用了这个形状。

senses.title: The top line of a roof
senses.definition: the horizontal line where two sloping roof surfaces meet at the top
senses.definitionCN: 两面坡屋顶在最上端相交的水平线
senses.example: Snow lay along the roof ridge like a white stripe.
senses.exampleCN: 积雪沿屋脊躺着，像一条白条。
senses.why: A roof is two slopes meeting at a line, exactly the geometry of a mountain ridge.
senses.whyCN: 屋顶是两面坡交于一条线，与山脊的几何形状完全一致。

senses.title: A long narrow bank of sand or ice
senses.definition: a narrow raised strip of sand, gravel or ice built by water, wind or glacier movement
senses.definitionCN: 由水、风或冰川运动堆成的狭长沙、砾或冰的隆起
senses.example: A low ridge of sand separated the two pools.
senses.exampleCN: 一道低矮的沙脊把两个水塘隔开。
senses.why: Any process that piles material into a line produces the same long raised form.
senses.whyCN: 凡是把物质堆成一条线的过程，都会造出同样的长隆起。

senses.title: A high-pressure ridge on a weather map
senses.definition: an elongated area of high pressure extending from a centre
senses.definitionCN: 从中心延伸出来的一条狭长高压区
senses.example: A ridge of high pressure brought a week of clear skies.
senses.exampleCN: 一条高压脊带来了一周的晴空。
senses.why: Meteorology draws pressure as terrain, so an elongated high becomes a ridge on the map.
senses.whyCN: 气象学把气压画成地形，于是一条狭长的高压区在图上就成了脊。

senses.title: A raised line between furrows
senses.definition: the raised strip of soil between two furrows in a field
senses.definitionCN: 田里两条沟之间隆起的土条
senses.example: The farmer planted beans along every ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 农民沿每一道田垄种豆子。
senses.why: Agriculture makes miniature ridges on purpose: a line of soil with two lower sides.
senses.whyCN: 农业有意造出微缩的脊：一条土线，两侧更低。

senses.title: An undersea mountain chain
senses.definition: a long raised chain of mountains on the ocean floor
senses.definitionCN: 海底绵长隆起的一条山脉
senses.example: The mid-ocean ridge runs for thousands of kilometres.
senses.exampleCN: 洋中脊绵延数千公里。
senses.why: The same line-making process works under water, so the same word names the sea-floor version.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「造线」过程在水下也起作用，同一个词于是也指海底的那一版。

senses.title: The raised line of the nose
senses.definition: the narrow raised line running down the middle of the nose
senses.definitionCN: 沿鼻子中部向下的一条窄隆起
senses.example: A small scar crossed the ridge of his nose.
senses.exampleCN: 一道小疤横过他鼻梁。
senses.why: Anatomy uses the back-line image literally: the nose is a narrow ridge on the face.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学直接使用「背线」意象：鼻子就是脸上一条窄脊。

senses.title: To form or furnish with a ridge
senses.definition: to build something into a raised line, or to fit a roof with a ridge
senses.definitionCN: 把某物做成隆起的线条，或给屋顶装上脊瓦
senses.example: Workers ridged the field before the rains came.
senses.exampleCN: 工人在雨季到来前给田起垄。
senses.why: The noun became a verb: to ridge something is to give it the shape the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：给某物起脊，就是赋予它名词所指的形状。

intro.en: Ridge is a native Old English word for a back or spine, later applied to any long raised line. The dates are approximate and the deeper root is uncertain.
intro.cn: ridge 是古英语本族词，原指背或脊柱，后来用于任何狭长隆起。年代为约数，更深词根不确定。

items.en: Old English hrycg meant 'back, spine' and also 'ridge of land'; the same word covered the body and the landscape from the start.
items.cn: 古英语 hrycg 意为「背、脊柱」，也指「地脊」；这个词从一开始就同时覆盖身体与地貌。

items.en: The reconstructed ancestor is *hrugja-, with relatives in Old Saxon hruggi, Dutch rug and German Rücken, all meaning 'back'.
items.cn: 重构的祖形为 *hrugja-，同族词有古撒克逊语 hruggi、荷兰语 rug 与德语 Rücken，都意为「背」。

items.en: A link to a root meaning 'to bend or curve' is sometimes suggested, but the reconstruction is not agreed and no single form can be given.
items.cn: 有人提出它与一个意为「弯、曲」的词根有关，但该重构并未取得共识，也无法给出唯一形式。

items.en: Middle English ridge kept both the body sense and the land sense; the roof sense is recorded by the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语 ridge 同时保留身体义与土地义；屋顶义见于 15 世纪。

items.en: The geological sense 'undersea chain' and the meteorological sense 'high-pressure ridge' are nineteenth- and twentieth-century technical extensions.
items.cn: 地质义「海底山脉」与气象义「高压脊」是 19 至 20 世纪的技术延伸。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): the Old English and Germanic layers are secure, but the pre-Germanic origin is disputed; the first dates given are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：古英语与日耳曼语层次可靠，但日耳曼语之前的来源有争议；所给首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group holds words that differ from ridge by one sound or letter; the second holds words for raised lines and tops.
note.cn: 第一组是与 ridge 差一个音或一个字母的词；第二组是表示隆起线条与顶部的词。

entries.definition: A structure carrying a road over water; it begins with /br/, while ridge begins with /r/.
entries.definitionCN: 跨水承载道路的结构；以 /br/ 开头，而 ridge 以 /r/ 开头。

entries.definition: To equip a ship or a machine, or a truck; it ends in /ɡ/, not /dʒ/.
entries.definitionCN: 给船或机器装配索具，或指卡车；结尾是 /ɡ/ 而非 /dʒ/。

entries.definition: To free oneself of something; it ends in /d/, not /dʒ/.
entries.definitionCN: 摆脱某物；结尾是 /d/ 而非 /dʒ/。

entries.definition: The past tense or adjective form of ridge; the extra /d/ marks grammar, not a new word.
entries.definitionCN: ridge 的过去式或形容词形式；多出的 /d/ 标记语法，不是新词。

entries.definition: The highest line of a ridge or wave; crest is the line itself, ridge is the whole raised mass under it.
entries.definitionCN: 山脊或波浪的最高线；crest 是那条线本身，ridge 是线下方整块隆起。

entries.definition: The backbone, or a sharp narrow ridge; it keeps the body image that ridge also started from.
entries.definitionCN: 脊柱，或尖锐狭窄的山脊；它保留了 ridge 同样起始于身体的意象。

entries.definition: A narrow shelf of rock projecting from a cliff; it is horizontal, not a line running uphill.
entries.definitionCN: 崖壁上突出的窄岩台；它是水平的，而不是向上延伸的线。

entries.definition: A long steep slope or cliff separating two levels; it is the face below a ridge, not the ridge top.
entries.definitionCN: 分隔两级的陡坡或长崖；它是脊下方的坡面，而不是脊顶。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Old English body sense, the real compounds and the technical extensions.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的古英语身体义、真实的复合词与技术延伸。

normal.en: Old English hrycg meant both 'back' and 'land ridge'.
normal.cn: 古英语 hrycg 同时指「背」与「地脊」。

normal.en: The family runs ridge, ridged, ridging, ridgeline, ridgeway.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ridge、ridged、ridging、ridgeline、ridgeway。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: mountain ridge, ridge line, roof ridge, high-pressure ridge.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 mountain ridge、ridge line、roof ridge、high-pressure ridge。

normal.en: A ridge is two slopes meeting at a line; a roof is the same geometry in wood.
normal.cn: 山脊是两面坡交于一条线；屋顶只是同样的几何形状换成了木头。

normal.en: Compare crest: the crest is the line, the ridge is the mass that carries it.
normal.cn: 对比 crest：crest 是那条线，ridge 是承载它的整块隆起。

abstract.en: Picture a blanket pulled up in the middle so a long fold stands along its length.
abstract.cn: 想象一条毯子从中间被提起，沿长度方向立起一道长褶。

abstract.en: Picture rain falling on both sides of a roof and running away in two directions.
abstract.cn: 想象雨水落在屋顶两面，然后分别向两个方向流走。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn on a map where every drop of rain must choose one side.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上画着一条线，每一滴雨都必须选择其中一侧。

examples.en: The ridge forms the border between the two river systems.
examples.cn: 这条山脊构成两个水系之间的分界。

examples.en: Tiles along the roof ridge were replaced after the storm.
examples.cn: 风暴过后，屋脊上的瓦被换掉了。

examples.en: A ridge of high pressure should keep the sky clear until Friday.
examples.cn: 一条高压脊应该会让天空晴到周五。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞（rui）+ 脊（ji）」—— 山背上那条瑞气升起的长长脊线 → 山脊

root: 古英语 hrycg「背、脊柱；地脊」，重构祖形为原始日耳曼语 *hrugja-；更深词根存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all share one line: a long raised back with two sides falling away, whether made of rock, tiles, sand, air pressure, soil, sea floor or bone.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一条线：一条两侧下落的狭长脊背，无论它由岩石、瓦片、沙、气压、土壤、海底还是骨头构成。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long narrow back with two slopes falling away on either side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条狭长的脊背，两侧各有一面坡向下落。

branches.en: BIG TERRAIN: mountain ridges and undersea chains are the same long fold at two scales.
branches.cn: 大地形：山脊与海底山脉是同一种长褶皱在两个尺度上的表现。

branches.en: BUILT ROOFS: two sloping surfaces meet along one line.
branches.cn: 人造屋顶：两面坡沿一条线相交。

branches.en: SMALL STRIPS: sand, ice and soil are piled into lines by water, wind or plough.
branches.cn: 小条带：沙、冰与土被水、风或犁堆成线。

branches.en: DRAWN WEATHER: an elongated high is mapped as a ridge.
branches.cn: 画出的天气：狭长高压区被画成一条脊。

branches.en: BODY AND ACTION: the nose keeps the original back image, and the verb gives the shape to anything.
branches.cn: 身体与动作：鼻梁保留最初的「背」意象，动词则把这一形状赋予任何东西。

intro.en: Ridge is a native stem that compounds freely with land, roof and weather words.
intro.cn: ridge 是本土词干，能与土地、屋顶与天气词自由复合。

latinIntro.en: No Latin etymon is recoverable: ridge is native Old English and Germanic, so the Latin entry list is empty by design.
latinIntro.cn: 无法追溯到拉丁词源：ridge 是古英语本族词，属日耳曼语，因此拉丁条目按规则留空。

items.example: The ridge divides the two valleys.
items.exampleCN: 这条山脊把两个山谷分开。

items.meaning: more than one ridge; he, she or it ridges
items.example: Three ridges run north to south.
items.exampleCN: 三道山脊由北向南延伸。

items.example: The field was ridged for drainage.
items.exampleCN: 这块田被起垄以便排水。

items.example: Ridging keeps the roots above the water.
items.exampleCN: 起垄让根系高于水面。

items.meaning: the line along the top of a ridge
items.example: The ridgeline was sharp against the sky.
items.exampleCN: 山脊线在天空下显得锋利。

items.meaning: an ancient path along a ridge
items.example: The ridgeway follows the old boundary.
items.exampleCN: 这条山脊古道沿着旧边界走。

items.meaning: the top line of a roof
items.example: The roof ridge needs new tiles.
items.exampleCN: 屋脊需要换新瓦。

items.meaning: an elongated band of high pressure
items.example: The high-pressure ridge blocked the rain.
items.exampleCN: 高压脊挡住了降雨。

items.example: New crust forms along the mid-ocean ridge.
items.exampleCN: 新地壳沿洋中脊形成。

definition_zh: 山谷；河谷；谷地；低谷；凹槽；天沟
definition_en: low land between hills or mountains, usually with a river; also a low period or a long hollow in an object
core_image: 两侧坡地向上退开，中间留下一道长长的低槽，水沿槽底向前流
scene: 村子贴着河岸铺开，两侧的坡地一直升到树林边缘。The valley narrows where the river cuts between two slopes.
sceneCN: 此处指「两侧高地之间由河流穿过的低地」（第 1 个义项：坡面夹出的长条低谷）；句意为河流在两面坡之间切过的地方，山谷变窄了。图中可辨识物件：河岸、沿坡而建的房屋、两侧上升的坡地、树林边缘。

pos.zh: 山谷；河谷；谷地；低谷；凹槽；屋顶天沟
谷地的（如 valley floor、valley wind）

derivatives.zh: 谷热（一种地方性真菌感染）

senses.title: Low land between slopes
senses.definition: a long area of lower ground lying between hills or mountains
senses.definitionCN: 位于丘陵或山地之间的狭长低地
senses.example: The valley narrows where the river cuts between two slopes.
senses.exampleCN: 河流在两面坡之间切过的地方，山谷变窄了。
senses.why: Latin vallis named a hollow between rises; the word profiles the low line between two higher sides.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 vallis 指高地之间的凹处；这个词勾勒的是两面高地之间那条低线。

senses.title: A river valley
senses.definition: a valley shaped and drained by a river running along its floor
senses.definitionCN: 由沿谷底流动的河流塑造并排水的山谷
senses.example: The river valley widens as it approaches the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 河谷在接近大海时变宽。
senses.why: Valleys and rivers make each other: water cuts the trough, and the trough guides the water.
senses.whyCN: 山谷与河流互相造就：水切出槽，槽又引导水。

senses.title: The settled valley as a region
senses.definition: the valley used with the definite article for the farming or urban area inside it
senses.definitionCN: 加定冠词时，指谷地内部的农业或城市地区
senses.example: The valley supplies most of the region's fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 这片谷地供应本地区大部分水果。
senses.why: People live on the floor, not on the slopes, so the name of the low line comes to mean the community there.
senses.whyCN: 人住在谷底而不是坡上，于是这条低线的名字转而指那里的聚居区。

senses.title: A low period in activity
senses.definition: a period when economic activity or mood is at its lowest
senses.definitionCN: 经济活动或情绪处于最低点的时期
senses.example: The industry went through a deep valley before recovering.
senses.exampleCN: 这个行业在复苏之前经历了一段深谷。
senses.why: A graph of activity rises and falls like terrain, so a minimum is a valley between two peaks.
senses.whyCN: 活动曲线像地形一样起伏，因此最低点就是两个峰之间的一道谷。

senses.title: A long hollow in an object
senses.definition: a long shallow groove or depression in a surface
senses.definitionCN: 表面上一道长而浅的凹槽
senses.example: Water collected in the valley between the two roof panels.
senses.exampleCN: 水积在两块屋面板之间的凹槽里。
senses.why: The shape travels from landscape to objects: anything with two raised sides and a low middle has a valley.
senses.whyCN: 这个形状从地貌走到物体上：凡是两边高、中间低的东西都有一道谷。

senses.title: The internal angle of a roof
senses.definition: the internal line where two sloping roof surfaces meet and water runs off
senses.definitionCN: 两面坡屋顶相交、雨水汇流的内侧线
senses.example: Leaves blocked the valley and rainwater came in.
senses.exampleCN: 落叶堵住了天沟，雨水渗了进来。
senses.why: A roof valley is the mirror image of a ridge: two slopes meet low instead of high.
senses.whyCN: 屋顶天沟是屋脊的镜像：两面坡在低处而不是高处相交。

senses.title: Attributive: of the valley
senses.definition: used before a noun to locate something on the valley floor or in valley air
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，表示位于谷底或在谷地空气中
senses.example: Valley winds rise in the afternoon and cool the orchards.
senses.exampleCN: 谷风在午后升起，给果园降温。
senses.why: The noun marks the setting, as English nouns often do when placed before another noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词标出场景，正如英语名词放在另一名词前时常做的那样。

senses.title: A rift valley in geology
senses.definition: a long trough formed where the earth's crust is pulled apart
senses.definitionCN: 地壳被拉开处形成的长条凹槽
senses.example: The rift valley is widening by a few centimetres each year.
senses.exampleCN: 这条裂谷每年加宽几厘米。
senses.why: Geology extends the shape to a trough made by tension rather than by a river.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把这一形状扩展到由张力而非河流造成的凹槽。

intro.en: Valley came through Old French from Latin vallis; the deeper origin is uncertain, and the dates are approximate.
intro.cn: valley 经古法语来自拉丁 vallis；更深来源不确定，年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin vallis, also written valles, meant 'valley, hollow'; it was a common word in land description and in military writing about ground between hills.
items.cn: 拉丁 vallis（也写作 valles）意为「谷、凹地」；它是描写地形的常用词，也见于军事文献中对丘间地面的记述。

items.en: The pre-Latin origin of vallis is not established. Suggestions linking it to a root for 'to fold' or to unrelated hollow words are hypotheses, not demonstrated derivations.
items.cn: vallis 在拉丁语之前的来源尚未确立。把它与表示「折」的词根或与无关的「凹」义词相联系的种种说法都只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Old French valee, later vallee, carried the word into English; the modern spelling valley was fixed in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 valee（后来作 vallee）把这个词带入英语；现代拼写 valley 在 16 世纪固定下来。

items.en: Middle English used the word for both the landform and the settled district inside it, a double sense that survives today.
items.cn: 中古英语既用这个词指地貌，也指地貌内部的聚居区，这一双重义保留至今。

items.en: The sense 'low period' is modern and belongs to the language of graphs and business cycles, where a minimum is drawn as a dip.
items.cn: 「低谷期」这一义项是现代用法，属于图表与商业周期的语言，在那里最低点被画成一个凹陷。

items.en: Source uncertain (root and first date): vallis has no agreed Indo-European source, and the earliest English citations are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：vallis 没有公认的印欧来源，最早的英语书证年代为约数。

note.en: The first group holds words that resemble valley in spelling or sound; the second holds words for low ground between higher sides.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写或读音与 valley 相似的词；第二组是表示两侧高地之间低地的词。

entries.definition: Worth or importance; the ending is -ue, not -ey, and the word has nothing to do with land.
entries.definitionCN: 价值或重要性；结尾是 -ue 而非 -ey，与土地无关。

entries.definition: A burst of shots or words; the first vowel is /ɒ/ in British English, not /æ/.
entries.definitionCN: 一阵齐射或连串话语；英式英语中首个元音是 /ɒ/ 而非 /æ/。

entries.definition: A literary word for a valley, from the same Latin vallis; it is a shorter cousin, not a misspelling.
entries.definitionCN: 文学语中表示山谷的词，同出拉丁 vallis；它是更短的近亲，不是拼写错误。

entries.definition: The plural of valley; the -s marks number, not a different word.
entries.definitionCN: valley 的复数；-s 标记数量，不是另一个词。

entries.definition: A narrow steep-sided valley, often with a river; it is much tighter and rockier than a broad valley.
entries.definitionCN: 狭窄陡壁的谷，常有河流；比宽阔的 valley 更窄、更多岩石。

entries.definition: A deep narrow valley with steep walls, cut by a river in dry country; its depth and walls are its defining features.
entries.definitionCN: 干旱地区由河流切出的深窄谷，陡壁是其核心特征。

entries.definition: A valley, especially in northern English place names; it is the native word beside the French-derived valley.
entries.definitionCN: 山谷，尤见于英格兰北部地名；它是与法语来源的 valley 并列的本族词。

entries.definition: A wide bowl of land drained by one river system; it is broad and rounded, not a long trough.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一水系排水的一片宽阔盆地；它宽而圆，不是长槽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin source, the real compounds and the shape contrast with ridge.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁来源、真实的复合词，以及与 ridge 的形状对照。

normal.en: Latin vallis 'valley' gives the stem vall-, also seen in vale.
normal.cn: 拉丁 vallis「谷」给出词干 vall-，也见于 vale。

normal.en: The family runs valley, valleys, valley floor, valley wall, valley breeze.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 valley、valleys、valley floor、valley wall、valley breeze。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: river valley, valley floor, in the valley.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 river valley、valley floor、in the valley。

normal.en: A ridge is high in the middle; a valley is low in the middle. Same two slopes, opposite join.
normal.cn: 山脊中间高，山谷中间低；同样的两面坡，相交的方向相反。

normal.en: A roof valley is the low join of two slopes, the mirror of a roof ridge.
normal.cn: 屋顶天沟是两面坡的低处交线，是屋脊的镜像。

abstract.en: Picture two hands held apart with a narrow gap between the palms.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手分开，掌心之间留出一道窄缝。

abstract.en: Picture a river that has spent a million years drawing one line downhill.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河用了一百万年，只为在谷底画出一条向下的线。

abstract.en: Picture an economic chart that dips between two high points.
abstract.cn: 想象一张经济图表，在两个高点之间凹下去。

examples.en: Morning fog often fills the valley until noon.
examples.cn: 晨雾常常填满山谷，一直到中午。

examples.en: The valley floor is covered with orchards and small fields.
examples.cn: 谷底布满果园和小块田地。

examples.en: The company survived a long valley before its next product succeeded.
examples.cn: 在下一个产品成功之前，公司熬过了一段漫长的低谷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挖（va）+ 里（lley）」—— 两边挖开，只留中间一条低槽 → 山谷

root: 古法语 valee ← 拉丁 vallis/valles「谷、凹地」；拉丁语之前的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all begin with two higher sides and a low middle: land, a river's course, a settled district, a low period, a groove, a roof gutter, a setting and a rift.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从「两边高、中间低」出发：地形、河道、聚居区、低谷期、凹槽、屋顶天沟、场景与裂谷。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two slopes withdrawing from a long low line that water follows.
core.cn: 核心意象：两面坡向后退开，中间留出一条水所遵循的长低线。

branches.en: LANDFORM AND WATER: the trough and the river that made it are one system.
branches.cn: 地形与水：凹槽与造就它的河流是同一个系统。

branches.en: THE PLACE PEOPLE USE: the floor is farmland, and the noun marks valley settings.
branches.cn: 人们使用的场所：谷底是农田，该名词也标出谷地场景。

branches.en: THE GRAPH: a minimum between two maxima is drawn as a valley.
branches.cn: 图表：两个最大值之间的最小值被画成一道谷。

branches.en: THE SHAPE IN OBJECTS: grooves and roof gutters repeat the two-high, one-low profile.
branches.cn: 物体中的形状：凹槽与天沟重复了「两边高、中间低」的轮廓。

branches.en: THE RIFT: tension, not water, can also open a long trough.
branches.cn: 裂谷：造成长槽的也可以是张力，而非水。

intro.en: Valley is a Romance loan with a stable stem; English mostly builds compounds rather than suffix derivatives on it.
intro.cn: valley 是词干稳定的罗曼语借词；英语主要在它上面造复合词，而非后缀派生词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vallis, also valles, supplies the stem; the native English synonym dale comes from a different Old English word and is not a Latin relative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vallis（亦作 valles）提供词干；英语本族同义词 dale 来自另一个古英语词，并非拉丁同族。

items.example: The stem vall- survives in vale and valley.
items.exampleCN: 词干 vall- 保存在 vale 与 valley 中。

items.structure: Old French valee, from Latin vallis
items.example: The valley runs east to west.
items.exampleCN: 这条山谷由东向西延伸。

items.example: Two valleys meet below the village.
items.exampleCN: 两条山谷在村下汇合。

items.meaning: the flat bottom of a valley
items.example: The valley floor is fertile.
items.exampleCN: 谷底土地肥沃。

items.meaning: the steep side of a valley
items.example: The valley wall rises sharply.
items.exampleCN: 谷壁陡峭上升。

items.meaning: a wind that rises up a valley slope
items.example: The valley breeze begins at midday.
items.exampleCN: 谷风在正午开始。

items.meaning: a fungal infection common in dry western valleys
items.meaningCN: 常见于西部干旱谷地的一种真菌感染
items.example: Valley fever cases rise after dusty winds.
items.exampleCN: 扬尘风之后谷热病例会增加。

items.structure: Latin vallis via Old French val
items.example: The vale lay green below the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 山脊下方的谷地一片翠绿。

latinEntries.structure: valles, vallis (f., third declension, variant of vallis)

definition_zh: 峡谷；深谷；海底峡谷；城市峡谷
definition_en: a deep narrow valley with steep sides, usually cut by a river; also a similar narrow passage between high walls
core_image: 河水在岩层里切出一条又深又窄的竖缝，两侧是几乎垂直的岩壁
scene: 河水在岩层里切出一条又深又窄的缝，站在边缘看不到底。The canyon drops three hundred metres from rim to river.
sceneCN: 此处指「河流在岩层中切出的深窄峡谷」（第 1 个义项：两壁陡直、深度远大于宽度的谷）；句意为从崖缘到河面，这条峡谷垂直下落三百米。图中可辨识物件：垂直岩壁、谷底河流、崖缘、看不到底的深度。

pos.zh: 峡谷；深谷（两壁陡直）；海底峡谷；城市峡谷

collocations.zh: 城市峡谷（高楼夹出的街道）

senses.title: A deep narrow river-cut valley
senses.definition: a deep valley with steep rock walls, cut by a river over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 由河流长期切割而成、两壁陡直的深谷
senses.example: The canyon drops three hundred metres from rim to river.
senses.exampleCN: 从崖缘到河面，这条峡谷垂直下落三百米。
senses.why: Spanish cañón named a tube or pipe; the word pictures a narrow channel with walls, not a broad valley.
senses.whyCN: 西班牙语 cañón 原指管子；这个词勾勒的是一条有壁的窄通道，而不是宽阔的谷。

senses.title: The canyon country as a region
senses.definition: a district characterised by many deep canyons, often used in place names
senses.definitionCN: 以众多深峡谷为特征的地带，常用于地名
senses.example: The canyon country attracts geologists every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这片峡谷地带每年春天都吸引地质学家。
senses.why: One canyon becomes a landscape when many of them define a whole district.
senses.whyCN: 当许多峡谷共同定义一整片地区时，一条峡谷就变成一种地貌景观。

senses.title: A submarine canyon
senses.definition: a steep-sided underwater valley cut into the continental slope
senses.definitionCN: 切入大陆坡的陡壁海底谷
senses.example: Sediment flows down the submarine canyon after storms.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后，沉积物沿海底峡谷向下流动。
senses.why: The same cutting process works under water, so the same word names the submerged form.
senses.whyCN: 同样的切割过程在水下也起作用，同一个词于是指被水淹没的那一版。

senses.title: An urban canyon
senses.definition: a street enclosed by tall buildings on both sides, studied for wind and heat effects
senses.definitionCN: 两侧被高楼夹住的街道，常被研究风与热效应
senses.example: The urban canyon traps heat until well after sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 这条城市峡谷把热量困住，直到日落后很久。
senses.why: Tall walls on both sides reproduce the geometry of a canyon, so city planning borrows the word.
senses.whyCN: 两侧高墙复制了峡谷的几何形状，于是城市规划借用了这个词。

senses.title: A narrow deep passage
senses.definition: a narrow gap between high walls, natural or artificial
senses.definitionCN: 高墙之间的狭窄缝隙，天然或人造皆可
senses.example: The trail squeezes through a canyon of broken rock.
senses.exampleCN: 小径从一条碎石夹成的窄缝中挤过去。
senses.why: Width and depth, not a river, are what the word really requires.
senses.whyCN: 这个词真正要求的是宽度与深度，而不是必须有河。

senses.title: A huge gap between positions
senses.definition: a very large separation between opinions, generations or groups
senses.definitionCN: 意见、代际或群体之间的巨大分隔
senses.example: A canyon separates the two sides of the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 一场辩论的两方之间隔着一道鸿沟。
senses.why: A deep gap in the ground becomes a deep gap in agreement: both are measured by distance across.
senses.whyCN: 地面的深缝变成意见上的深缝：两者都用「跨越的距离」来衡量。

senses.title: Attributive: of a canyon
senses.definition: used before a noun for the walls, rim or floor of a canyon
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，指峡谷的壁、缘或底
senses.example: Canyon walls record millions of years of rock layers.
